chief_complaint: facial malar rash, joint pain, and hair loss
hpi_details: A 26-year-old female presents to the clinic with facial malar rash, joint pain, and hair loss. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks the facial redness and thinning hair are an allergic reaction to a new cosmetic cream or an extreme sensitivity to sunlight.
concerns: She is worried that the rash will permanently scar her face and that her hair will fall out before her sister's upcoming wedding.
expectations: She hopes to receive a soothing medicated skin cream and vitamins to stop her hair from falling out.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Check ANA/dsDNA, initiate Hydroxychloroquine and low-dose steroids, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Dermatomyositis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Kidney involvement signs.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of facial malar rash, joint pain, and hair loss. HPI: autoantibody immune complex deposition.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
reference_soap.plan: Evaluate with targeted testing rather than ANA alone: CBC, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis with microscopy and urine protein quantification, complements, anti-dsDNA, and other serology as clinically indicated. Reduced urine output, edema/foamy urine, hypertension, neurologic symptoms, chest pain/dyspnea, or severe illness needs urgent same-day assessment for organ-threatening disease. Rheumatology should direct hydroxychloroquine, glucocorticoids, or immunosuppressants with pregnancy planning, eye screening, infection review, and laboratory monitoring.

must_ask.say: Does your rash follow a butterfly pattern across your cheeks?
Does sunlight make the rash worse?

history.answer: I came in because I developed this red rash across my cheeks and nose, and lately my joints have been aching and my hair is falling out.
The redness on my cheeks started about three weeks ago, and over the past week it has gradually gotten redder and spread across the bridge of my nose.
It is across both of my cheeks and the bridge of my nose like a butterfly shape, but it completely skips the folds next to my mouth. I do not have rashes on my hands, feet, or body folds.
It is a flat reddish rash with some slightly raised patches, but there are no blisters, pus bumps, flaking, or crusting.
It does not itch, but it feels slightly warm and sensitive when touched. I had no pain or tingling before the rash broke out.
No, it stays on my face all the time once it appears. It does not disappear within a few hours or move to other places like hives.
I have never had a facial rash or joint problems like this before in my life.
I have felt completely exhausted and run-down lately. I have not had high fevers or shaking chills, just an occasional warm feeling.
Now that you mention it, I noticed two small painless sores on the roof of my mouth last week. I do not have any eye redness or sores around my private area.
No, my skin is not blistering or sloughing off at all, and I have not seen any dark purple spots that do not fade when pressed.
No, my lips and tongue have never swollen, and I have not had any shortness of breath, throat tightness, or dizziness.
No, I have not started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, gout medications, or anti-seizure pills.
No, I have not changed my face cream, makeup, sunscreen, or laundry detergent, and I have not worn new jewelry or handled wild plants.
No, my roommate does not have any rash, itching, or similar symptoms.
No, I have not been bitten by ticks or bugs, I have not gone hiking or traveling recently, and I have not visited public pools or saunas.
No, I have never had atopic dermatitis, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
Both of my wrists and finger joints have been aching and feeling stiff, especially when I wake up in the morning. My fingernails and toenails look normal without pitting or discoloration.
I tried putting an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream on my face for two days, but it did not make any difference so I stopped.
I have a steady boyfriend and we consistently use condoms. I have never had genital ulcers, abnormal discharge, or any sexually transmitted infections.
Yes, over the past few weeks clumps of hair have been coming out whenever I shower or brush my hair, and it is visibly thinning all over.
Yes, definitely. Last weekend I spent about an hour outside in the sun, and the redness on my cheeks became much more intense and burned afterward.
No, my urine looks normal with no foam or blood, I have not had any drop in urine amount, and my ankles are not swollen.
I thought maybe I was having a bad allergic reaction to a new facial cleanser or developed an extreme sun allergy.
I'm terrified that this rash is going to permanently scar my face and that I'll lose all my hair before my sister's wedding.
I have always been healthy and do not have any chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I do not take any regular prescription medications or herbal supplements, only occasional acetaminophen for mild headaches.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink alcohol socially, about one glass of wine once or twice a month.
I work as an administrative assistant in an office and live in an apartment with a roommate.
My mother has Hashimoto thyroiditis, but no one in my family has lupus, kidney disease, or other autoimmune conditions.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my cycles are regular every 28 days without unusual bleeding.
We use condoms reliably every time, and there is no chance that I could be pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 37.0°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert and oriented, appears mildly fatigued, in no acute distress, with visible diffuse thinning of scalp hair.
Confluent erythematous maculopapular rash across the nasal bridge and bilateral cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds, blanching on pressure, without scarring or discoid plaques.
Conjunctivae are clear without injection or pallor, sclerae anicteric, and no periorbital edema or heliotrope discoloration.
Two small, shallow, non-tender mucosal ulcerations on the hard palate with otherwise clear oropharynx.
No cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy palpated.
Regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, with no murmurs, gallops, or pericardial friction rub.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with no crackles, wheezes, or pleural friction rub.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without palpable hepatosplenomegaly.
Mild tenderness and subtle soft-tissue swelling over bilateral proximal interphalangeal joints, metacarpophalangeal joints, and wrists, with preserved range of motion and no joint deformities.
No pretibial pitting edema on either lower extremity, and peripheral pulses are intact bilaterally.
